thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU pool eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3: capacity_exhaustion detected (queue_growth) -> queue length rising above 500. alert level: P1.

sylvie: taking pager — oncall SRE. Looking now.

raj: I'm seeing autoscaler flapping in metrics, attempts to scale -> hit max_replicas for the pool (12).

marta: logs show many small requests pinned to large-MIG configs. Possible fragmentation: a bunch of 7g.20gb MIG slices blocked by binpack.

jamie: customer impact? Which tenants affected?

kevin: support banner: customers with high-qps routes are seeing 503s and queueing. Reported: acme-inc models and nl-analytics embedding jobs.

incident-bot: Detected: queue_length=612, avg_latency=2.8s (up from 0.18s), gpu_util=98%, pending_requests=430. Autoscaler events: 8 scale-up attempts in last 5m, 6 failures due to placement constraints.

sylvie: quick triage — suspected MIG sizing mismatch + fragmentation causing stranded GPU slices. If pool can't get additional homogeneous slices, autoscaler refuses to place.

raj: confirming: node-level logs show "no matching device profile" for pending pods. Repacking didn't run because repacker backlog is high.

marta: suggest immediate mitigations: 1) enable burstpool for this pool (gives temporary oversubscribe), 2) route low-tier traffic to smaller model variant, 3) manual evict of long-lived low-priority jobs occupying large slots.

jamie: I'll draft comms. kevin, can you surface top 5 customer requesters and approximate impact severity?

kevin: acme-inc: heavy gen routes -> 40% failed; nl-analytics: embedding batch jobs delayed; internal staging runs also stalled. I'll message affected customers now and add status page notice. :frowning_face:

deploy-bot: Automated action suggestion: toggle burstpool for eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3? run: ``redwoodctl pools burst enable eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 --duration 15m``

sylvie: do it. jamie, go-ahead with customer note: "temporary throttling and longer queue times".

raj: running diagnostics, posting relevant snippets:
```
# pod scheduling failures (excerpt)
FailedScheduling: 0/18 nodes are available: 12 node(s) didn't match device profile, 6 InsufficientGPU.
autoscaler: attempt_scale_up(max_replicas=12) -> placement_error: fragmented_mig_sets
```

marta: adding: metrics show the majority of pending pods request MIG type a100-7g-20GB, but pool currently has many 1g-8GB slices which can't host them -> stranded capacity.

sylvie: manual steps I'm executing now:
- mark pool read-only for new deployments
- enable burstpool for 20m (grants temporary mixed packing)
- baja: lower concurrency for non-prod routes

jamie: comms posted: "We are investigating GPU capacity issues in eu-west. Some requests may see increased latency or 503s. We're applying mitigations now." (status.redwood.ai updated)

kevin: customers notified. acme flagged for escalation if no improvement in 15m.

deploy-bot: Running command: ``redwoodctl pools burst enable eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 --duration 20m --reason "incident 4781236540"``

incident-bot: burstpool enable accepted. Rebalance trigger queued.

raj: burstpool applied. Starting eviction of long-lived low-priority pods:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp,PRI:.metadata.annotations/priority
# evicting candidates
for p in $(kubectl get pods ...); do kubectl delete pod $p --grace-period=5; done
```

marta: also rolling fallback policy: route model-large -> model-medium for tier=free and tier=internal to reduce big slot requests. Adding routing rule now.

sylvie: seeing queue dropping: 612 -> 220 in 6m. avg_latency -> 1.1s. gpu_util -> 92%. progress.

jamie: can we open temporary extra capacity (dedicated) from dedicated pool eu-west-1-spare-2? That pool has 3 compatible slices but will require approval.

raj: manual allocation requires infra approval; I'll request immediate borrow: ``allocctl borrow eu-west-1-spare-2 -> eu-west-1-gpu-pool-3 --count 3``. Running request.

marta: note for postmortem: repacker backlog + conservative autoscaler placement policy + rigid MIG assignment are root causes. Need adaptive fallback to allow partial placement onto mixed MIGs when queue big and latency SLO broken.

kevin: acme wants ETA on full restoration. We can say "partial mitigation in place, risk reduced; full normalization in 1-2 hours while repacker finishes".

incident-bot: allocation request acknowledged. approval needed from infra-leads.

raj: got manual approval from infra-lead on call, borrowing 3 nodes. patching pool config now.

sylvie: after borrow, queue down to 48, latency back to normalish 0.24s, errors reduced to <1%. Marking P1 -> watching.

jamie: updating incident channel + status page: "mitigations applied, customers affected see reduced errors; investigating long-term fix."

kevin: customers acknowledged — acme keeping support channel open but happy with improvement.

marta: scheduling postmortem and action items:
- relax placement strictness under sustained queue growth (owner: eng-runtime)
- increase repacker throughput / prioritization (owner: eng-sre)
- revisit default MIG sizing for new deployments (owner: infra)
- add automated fallback routing to smaller model variants (owner: product)

sylvie: handoff to oncall runbook: monitor for 2h, escalate if queue >100 or error rate >2% for 5m. I'll stay on for the next 30m then hand to raj if stable.

raj: acknowledged, taking long-watch after sylvie.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged -> status: mitigated. Thread closed when last_message_ts reached.

sylvie: thanks team. Filing preliminary incident note. We'll review in postmortem. :thumbsup:
